background.definition: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) consists of a broad spectrum of neuromuscular disorders of variable severity, with onset from infancy to early adulthood.

list.listitem: One in 10,000 worldwide; 1 in 40 to 60 is a carrier.

An Italian database study estimated a prevalence of 5.1 per 100,000 when combining certain, probable and possible cases. It was 1.1/100,000 when limited to certain cases, and the annual incidence was 0.11 to 0.56/100,000/year.
A US database study gathering data from 2018 to 2022 identified 6,244,825 infants of whom 425 had a confirmed diagnosis of spinal muscular atrophy, a rate of 1 in 14,694.
Genetic cause of motor neuron loss that leads to proximal muscle weakness and disability; severe forms lead to early childhood death from respiratory failure.
Werdnig-Hoffman disorder is the most severe form, with onset at birth or early infancy.
Kugelberg-Welander disorder is a mild form, with onset in adolescence.
Autosomal recessive hereditary disorder.
Homogeneous deletion of SMN1 causes 95% phenotypic expression.
A similar gene SMN2 has an inverse relation of genotypic and phenotypic expression.
X-linked disorders leading to SMA have been identified.
Routine prenatal screening is not routinely recommended in the US or Europe. C

However, a non-randomized trial took advantage of a screening pilot project in 2 German federal states. The screening program identified 44 children, compared with 190 in the clinical symptom onset cohort. Treatment with disease-modifying drugs was initiated earlier in the screening cohort (1.3 months versus 10.7 months) and children in the screening cohort were more likely to gain the ability to sit independently (90.9% vs 74.2%). Independent ambulation was present in 64% in the screening group and 15% in the clinical onset group.
Genetic testing of parents may be useful to predict future offspring risk, but only if the affected child is tested positive for the gene deletion. C
Failure to attain motor milestones should initiate afn investigation for neuromuscular disorders, including SMA. B
Gross motor function testing may be used to evaluate the effectiveness of treatments or therapies. C

Differential.Differential_Features: Sensory impairment noted with the motor deficit
Acute onset and affecting extraocular and sphincter muscles
Hepatomegaly, macroglossia, and cardiomegaly seen in Pompe disease
Muscle biopsy with severe atrophy in SMA

list.listitem: Infants presenting with difficulty swallowing or sitting unaided by 6 months of age should be evaluated.
Inability of a toddler between the ages of 12 to 36 months to walk unaided or development of proximal muscle weakness may be an indicator of SMA, type 2.
Standing unaided, but with difficulty standing from a seated position, may be an early sign of Kugelberg-Welander disorder.
If SMA is clinically suspected, order the homozygous SMN1 exon 7 deletion test. Sensitivity is approximately 95% and specificity is 99% (LR+ 95, LR– 0.05).
A newer test under investigation is high-resolution DNA melting analysis (HRMA) with saturation LC Green dyes; in 1 study, HRMA identified patients with SMA with 100% clinical sensitivity.

Hemizygous SMN1 exon 7 deletion test and SMN1 subtle mutation screening are indicated for patients with clinical disease. Genetic testing will assist in counseling the patient's family in production of further offspring or risk of the disease in first-degree relatives.
Gross motor function testing is used to follow outcomes of treatment in children during clinical trials.
Electromyelogram studies are useful to confirm the abnormality in nerve conduction.
Muscle sonography can differentiate SMA from muscular dystrophies by findings of heterogeneous muscle fibers and severe atrophy.
Suspect SMA in infants presenting with floppy limbs, difficulty in suckling or swallowing, or any impairment of breathing. Children present with difficulty in attaining motor milestones.
Initial evaluation should consist of focused neurological and motor testing and detailed accounts of family history of neuromuscular disease.
Proactive supportive care has been shown to improve survival. B
Gastrostomy tube placement and Nissen fundoplication coupled with noninvasive positive pressure ventilation may improve nutrition and quality of life in patients with severe SMA. C
Gene replacement therapy, B risplidam, and nusinersen A are important new therapies for spinal muscular atrophy.

Nusinersen is a modified antisense olignucleotide. It modifies splicing of pre-messenger RNA and increases expression of the SMN protein whose deficiency is the cause of SMN. A systematic review of three recent RCTs concluded that it improved motor function in children with late onset SMA, and mortality and motor function in infants with infantile onset SMA.

Risdiplam also modifies SMN2 pre-messenger RNA splicing and thereby increases levels of SMN protein in patients with spinal muscular atrophy. A study comparing risdiplam with untreated historical controls found better motor function and motor milestone response in infants treated with risdiplam.

Gastrostomy tube placement and Nissen fundoplication coupled with noninvasive positive pressure ventilation may improve nutrition and quality of life in patients with severe SMA, especially in patients with difficulty swallowing and risk of aspiration.
A small quasi-experimental study compared low dose gene replacement therapy and high-dose gene replacement therapy with historical controls and found improved survival and better motor function.
Physical therapy may be used for symptomatic needs relating to contractures or to limit deconditioning during hospitalizations.
Noninvasive ventilation has been shown to improve survival in Werdnig-Hoffman disorder.

In a German cohort study of 66 children with SMA born between 2000 and 2005, 4 had severe SMA type '0' (1 SMN2 copy) with joint contractures and respiratory distress from birth. Median age at diagnosis in 57 patients with 2 SMN2 copies was 1.2 months and 3.5 months in the 5 patients with 3 SMN2 copies. Median age at death was 6.5 months in patients with 2 SMN2 copies. All patients with 3 SMN2 copies were still alive at 10 months to 55 months, 2 of them on permanent ventilation.
Long-term survival in Werdnig-Hoffman disorder is related to the need to treat multiple associated illnesses of chronic disease. B
Quality of life in patients with Kugelberg-Welander disorder may be related to access to ancillary services, such as physical therapy. C
